logline: Bloodlines starts with a man asking permission to inherit stars and ends with him warning everyone: the ancestors' gifts turn out to be the blood already in his hands.
reading:
The poem runs on a refrain of permission: 'They tell me to ask' if he can inherit the earth, name his own stars, invent a universe, and ask if God would let 'little old me' hand out a blessing. Facts sit between the asks: he came of age in shared basement rooms used as bedrooms, on mattress pads under southern pine beams that 'could comfort my spine, it didn't.' Each stanza ends on 'To dream was to prevail', so dreaming here means surviving, not escaping. Tears 'spoke in lieu of forbidden lines', and the history is 'too battered and bruised to travel.'

The poem turns on 'Their blood flows through my hands.' He stops asking: what he was told to ask for is already in his body. His fingerprints 'orchestra great powers', the sun kisses his skin, and his voice drops to 'a baritone of a million cries', one voice carrying many. The last line turns the petitioner into a power: 'Beware of me.' The governing images are lights held in hands (star, galaxy, universe), the low pine ceiling over a thin pad on concrete, palms and fingerprints, and a voice that is a chorus.
motifs: the refrain 'they tell me to ask': permission sought, then not needed
lights small enough to hold: star, galaxy, universe in cupped palms
southern-pine joists low over a thin pad on concrete
'To dream was to prevail', said twice as the hinge
naming stars after kin: a constellation that is a family
blood and fingerprints: the hands as the inheritance
one voice holding a million cries (baritone, chorus)
the petitioner turned power: 'Beware of me'

light_and_texture: In the field, the props are the light: lantern-gold and star-white glow on indigo kraft. The sky is a black card pricked with holes and backlit, and each puppet gets a warm rim on the side facing the parade. The ancestors' robes are gouache kente on corrugated card with gold foil on staff caps, galaxy rims and neck rings. The basement is a separate, colder shoebox: grey fluted card for cinderblock, real pine-coloured kraft strips for joists, and two or three drifting tracing-paper sheets for the humid haze, lit flat and blue from the window well.

best_elements.label: field of lights at dusk
best_elements.use: far/mid plate for 05.1a and 05.3a: the night field the parade crosses
best_elements.why: No figure in it, so it won't fight the puppet. A low horizon leaves sky for stars and the gate, and the glowing points already read as lanterns.

best_elements.label: Ascent: cosmic arches over the parade
best_elements.use: plate for the rendered passage (05_L17) and 05.4b; the arch column is where the archive opens
best_elements.why: Broad vertical stone faces beside the path, and a parade already small and deep in frame. It is the only plate where cosmos and procession share one image.

best_elements.label: starry kente ancestors (G0)
best_elements.use: costume and palette reference for ancestor_robe_indigo_gold; cropped far layer for 'a million cries'
best_elements.why: It shows the afro-futurist robe with the night sky inside the cloth, which tells the painters exactly what to paint.

best_elements.label: red-gold kente, arms raised (G2)
best_elements.use: reference for the ancestor 'raises galaxy overhead' pose and the blessing hand
best_elements.why: Bright, large gesture with a clear open palm. The colour sets the kente magenta/gold.

best_elements.label: ringed hands among white blooms
best_elements.use: insert before 05.4a: his hands in a field of cotton-white flowers, cut to the painted palm card
best_elements.why: Hands are the poem's subject. The white bolls quietly carry the southern history without anyone saying it.

best_elements.label: lit spine under a red/black jacket
best_elements.use: 2 s cutaway on 'could comfort my spine, it didn't' (05_L06)
best_elements.why: Almost the poet's own red-piped costume. A literal glowing spine makes the line visible.

best_elements.label: glowing veins and ribs
best_elements.use: reference for blood_light_veins: how far the light should travel up the arm
best_elements.why: Warm amber light in the vessels, readable at small size.

best_elements.label: Gateways to the Mind (1958): branching lines
best_elements.use: archive insert that fills the palm card's lifeline on 'Their blood flows through my hands'
best_elements.why: Bright, big, organic branching that looks like blood and like roots, and it reads inside a hand-shaped mask.

best_elements.label: All My Babies (1953): woman on an iron bed
best_elements.use: the past 'waiting': it opens in the basement window well (05.2)
best_elements.why: A real southern Black home interior from the period: poor room, iron bed, waiting posture. That is exactly the memory the lines name.

best_elements.label: Snow Queen (1959): stars in window panes
best_elements.use: window_well_starlight: the named stars still visible from the basement
best_elements.why: A gridded pane full of points of light, a vertical surface that reads strongly in a dark set.

best_elements.label: two ghost figures in blue haze
best_elements.use: basement memory: the ancestors standing in the haze by the window ('the past too was waiting for me')
best_elements.why: It already has the humid blue-haze light we need, and the figures read as presences, not actors.

best_elements.label: Wings for Roger Windsock: drawn wings
best_elements.use: design source for the gate's wing leaves; plays inside the gate seam on 'Beware of me'
best_elements.why: Big flat white wings drawn in line, the same graphic language as our cards.

best_elements.label: white marble city on still water
best_elements.use: atlantis_glow_far through the opened gate (05.5c) and the hand-off to 06
best_elements.why: Marble and water match 06's opening line. It is calm and figure-free.

best_elements.label: Parade in New York: lights at night
best_elements.use: farthest layer of the parade coming over the rise (05.1a)
best_elements.why: Real procession lights at night. They sit under the painted lanterns without competing.

gaps: Every POET and ANCESTOR pack is still an unpainted layout. The ancestor sheets have no face reference, and the style strip shows only the poet's heads, so painters will clone his face. We need elder, woman and youth faces of several ages.

No basement plate exists. Every gen bedroom is a high-rise room with a city window. We must generate a low concrete room with cinderblock, raw southern-pine joists, a window well and a pad on the floor.
No winged marble gate anywhere in gen/views. Build it as a layered card (two hinged wing leaves) rather than hunt for it.
Lying replacement bodies (on the back from top down; on the side in profile) on the mattress pad. The replacement sheet has the cells but they are empty.
An extreme-close palm card (about 40 cm) with painted fingerprint whorls and a cut lifeline channel for the archive insert.
Ancestor poses the action sheet lacks: hand on the shoulder of the one in front (05.4b chain), arms open in welcome, staff raised while walking.

Archive of southern Black domestic life, 1930s-50s (basement or shared rooms, revival or homecoming processions, choirs). The passage answer 'Show 'Em the Road' (1954) has no thumbnail in our set to judge.
Sound: a male choir or low hum to stack under 'a baritone of a million cries'.

fx.how: Black card pricked with a needle in three hole sizes, backlit. The named stars are bigger holes with a tissue disc behind.
A soft gold radial gradient (code) on each lantern card with a 2-3% flicker; nothing glows on the bodies but a rim line.
Star card with an additive bloom; underlight the face card with a gold gradient mask from the chin up.
Letterpress-style names (AMOS, IDA, OTIS, RUTH, MAE) typed one letter per 3 frames beside each risen star, in a cream typewriter face.
A thin gold thread drawn on between the named stars (code stroke, slight wobble, like real thread).
Two or three tracing-paper sheets drifting slowly at different depths, lit blue; condensation dots on the window well card.
A cool shaft (soft polygon) from the well onto the pad; the two named stars visible in the pane.
Code-drawn node-and-filament web growing outward from the sphere card past the frame; nodes are paper dots.
A fingertip touch makes a four-point cross flare (cut paper star) on a node; one node swells into a thin gold card ring.
Red-gold veins painted on an overlay card wiped on from the ancestors' fingertips into his palm; the Gateways to the Mind (1958) archive plays inside the lifeline channel.
The whorl rings on the palm card light outward one ring at a time, on the beat of 'orchestra'.
A dawn-gold gradient sweeping across one side of his face card from frame right.
Shake the plate and set layers, not the puppet, on 'Beware of me': 6 frames, decaying.
The wing leaves rotate on their hinge brads. Concentric pale rings ripple across the stone (code), timed to sung notes.

passage.keep: It is the right line, the title and the turn from asking to having. Hands that open and stay open is one clear held gesture, and the inner face of an Ascent arch is a tall vertical surface, the kind that reads best. The 1954 'Boy and the road, both were in his blood' answers the line almost word for word and points ahead to the walk to the gate.
passage.better: In view_068, crop to the left arch column and darken the bonfire and crowd 30% so the film owns the brightest area; make the archive pane at least a third of frame height. Use the head-down replacement card, not a tilt. Leave his palms empty but add the faint red-gold vein overlay on 'blood', so the gift visibly enters the hands before the archive answers. Add the shoulder-chain ancestor's hand on his shoulder in the near layer to tie the shot to 05.4b.
alt_lines: 05_L06 'of southern pine could comfort my spine, it didn't.': a flat_push hand that stops (he pushes off the pad and stays half-raised); the window well pane above him opens on All My Babies (1953).

05_L02 'to ask if I can name my own stars': object held out, the star_orb raised at full reach; the galaxy disc in the ancestor's hands beside him opens on Heavenly Bodies (arch_a1aff56f) or a planetarium film.
05_L14 'in tears that spoke in lieu of forbidden lines': head lowers (replacement down card); the cinderblock wall face opens on archive of a classroom or a hand writing, and the writing stops.
05_L22 'Beware of me.': head down to stern-front swap; the seam of the winged gate opens on Wings for Roger Windsock (arch_f21b1a54) as the leaves part.

ideas: The basement as a shoebox diorama: pine joists stamped AMOS, IDA, OTIS, RUTH, MAE sag toward the lying puppet, and the window well plays All My Babies (1953, arch_8f8f18e8): the past 'waiting'.

Hands relay: gen_d4f10148b2 (hands among white blooms) cuts on the same frame to the painted palm card; the lifeline channel fills with Gateways to the Mind (1958, arch_318310a9) as 'their blood flows'.
Spine cut: on 'it didn't', 2 s of gen_d3b111555f (lit spine in a red/black jacket) between two frames of the restless puppet on the pad, then back to the profile 'sad' card.
Parade over the rise: gen_bad0cf8d7a as plate, Parade in New York (arch_1044618d) lights in the farthest layer, cut-out ancestors on a rail in front: three materials, one procession.
A million cries: the starry ancestors of gen_94cb9b924e printed on tracing paper as a translucent wall behind the profile puppet while the baritone line plays; the layer brightens with each phrase.
Naming stars: the puppet lifts the star_orb; it rises, a letterpress name types out, and a gold thread links it to the last one, ending on a constellation in the shape of the ancestor line.
Gate to 06: the wing leaves (drawn after arch_f21b1a54) part and gen_69ee5bb28b's white city on water shows through the seam, which becomes the first frame of 06.
